parts.article:
A unique golden textile
 
A two-man project to use spider silk is achieved after 4 years
 
A A rare textile made from the silk of more than a million wild spiders has been on display at the American Museum of Natural History in New York City. To produce this golden cloth, 70 people spent four years collecting golden-orb spiders from telephone poles in Madagascar, while another dozen workers carefully extracted about 80 feet of silk filament from each of the arachnids. The resulting 11-foot-by-4-foot textile is the only large piece of cloth made from natural spider silk in the world today.
 
B Spider silk is very elastic and strong compared with steel or Kevlar, said textile expert Simon Peers, who co-led the project. Kevlar is a lightweight synthetic fabric, chemically related to nylon, that is used in bullet-proof vests. Kevlar is resistant to wear, tear and heat and has virtually no melting point. But the tensile strength of spider silk is even greater than Kevlar’s aramid filaments and higher than that of high-grade steel. Most importantly, spider silk is extremely lightweight: a strand long enough to circle the Earth would weigh less than 500 grams (18 oz). It is also especially ductile, able to stretch up to 140 percent of its length without breaking and to retain its strength below –40 °C, giving it toughness equal to that of leading commercial fibres.
 
C Researchers have long been intrigued by the unique properties of spider silk. Unfortunately, spider silk is extremely hard to mass-produce. Unlike silkworms—easy to raise in captivity—spiders have a habit of biting off each other’s heads when housed together. According to Peers, there is intensive research worldwide aimed at replicating spider-silk tensile properties for use in medicine and industry, but no-one has yet reproduced all the qualities of natural silk.
 
D Peers conceived the idea of weaving spider silk after reading about French missionary Jacob Paul Camboué, who worked with spiders in Madagascar during the 1880s and 1890s. Camboué built a small hand-driven machine to extract silk from up to 24 spiders at once, without harming them: the spiders were briefly restrained, their silk collected, then released. Peers built a replica of this 24-spider “silking” machine, said co-leader Nicholas Godley. As a test the pair collected about 20 spiders. “When we stuck them in the machine and started turning it, lo and behold, this beautiful gold-coloured silk started coming out,” Godley recalled.
 
E To make a textile of any significant size, the scale had to increase dramatically. Fourteen thousand spiders yield about an ounce of silk, Godley said, and the finished textile weighs about 2.6 pounds. By the end, handlers had worked with more than one million female golden-orb spiders—abundant in Madagascar and famed for their golden thread. Because the spiders produce silk only in the rainy season, all were collected between October and June. An additional 12 workers used hand-powered machines to extract the silk and twist it into 96-filament yarn. After “silking”, the spiders were released; within a week they regenerate their silk, allowing the same individuals to be used again—“the gift that never stops giving,” said Godley.
 
F Spending four years to produce a single piece of cloth is hardly practical for scientists or companies hoping to exploit spider silk in biomedicine or as a Kevlar alternative. Several groups have inserted spider genes into bacteria and even goats to make silk, but results have been only partly successful. One reason is that spider silk begins as a liquid protein produced in a special gland in the abdomen. Using the spinneret, the spider applies force that rearranges the protein’s molecular structure, transforming it into solid fibre. “When we talk about a spider spinning silk, we’re talking about how it applies forces to convert liquid to solid,” explained spider-silk expert Todd Blackledge of the University of Akron, who was not involved in the project. “Every year we get closer to mass production, but we’re not there yet.” For now, we must be content with one extraordinarily beautiful cloth—courtesy of more than a million spiders.

reference:
Q14

解析 A段着重介绍了这是一块由一百多万只蜘蛛丝制成的、目前世界上唯一（only large piece）的大型天然蜘蛛丝织物，强调了它的独特性和艺术价值 。

句子 (Paragraph A) The resulting 11-foot-by-4-foot textile is the only large piece of cloth made from natural spider silk in the world today.

干扰 虽然这段提到了收集蜘蛛的过程（70 people... collecting），但核心并不是强调“需要的资源（iv）”，而是强调最终成果是稀有的艺术珍品 。

Q15

句子 (Paragraph B) Spider silk is very elastic and strong compared with steel or Kevlar... Most importantly, spider silk is extremely lightweight... It is also especially ductile...

干扰 不要选“scientific analysis（vi）”，因为这一段只是在描述它的“性质/属性”，并没有深入分析它是如何在生物学层面形成的（那是F段的内容）。

解析 B段整段都在罗列蜘蛛丝的物理特性，比如非常有弹性（elastic）、强韧（strong）、轻便（lightweight）以及延展性好（ductile） 。

Q16

句子 (Paragraph C) Unfortunately, spider silk is extremely hard to mass-produce. Unlike silkworms—easy to raise in captivity—spiders have a habit of biting off each other's heads when housed together.

干扰 你可能看到“intensive research”，就想选“textile industry（iii）”或“scientific analysis（vi）”，但本段主旨是解释为什么无法像养蚕那样大规模养殖蜘蛛。

解析 C段指出蜘蛛丝很难量产，因为蜘蛛如果被关在一起（in captivity），有互相咬掉脑袋（biting off each other's heads）的习惯，这正是养殖的难处 。

Q17

句子 (Paragraph D) Peers conceived the idea of weaving spider silk after reading about French missionary Jacob Paul Camboué... Peers built a replica of this 24-spider "silking" machine...

干扰 不要被“scientific analysis”迷惑，这里讲的是历史故事和一个机械装置的复原，重点在于“复活旧点子（old idea）”。

解析 D段提到 Peers 是读到了19世纪法国传教士 Camboué 的旧事迹后产生了灵感，并制造了一个复刻版（replica）的机器来试验这个老想法 。

Q18

句子 (Paragraph E) Fourteen thousand spiders yield about an ounce of silk... handlers had worked with more than one million female golden-orb spiders...

干扰 虽然提到了“rainy season（雨季）”，但这只是收集资源的一个限制条件，段落核心在于强调为了产出这块布所付出的庞大“数量”和“人力”。

解析 E段列举了为了完成这个项目所投入的巨大资源：14,000只蜘蛛才产一盎司丝，总共用了一百多万只蜘蛛，还有数十名工人长时间劳作 。

Q19

干扰 不要看到“genes”和“bacteria”就只关注“advances（iii）”，本段后半部分详细分析了“从液体变固体”的生物物理过程，这才是“科学分析”。

句子 (Paragraph F) One reason is that spider silk begins as a liquid protein... the spider applies force that rearranges the protein's molecular structure, transforming it into solid fibre.

解析 F段深入解释了蜘蛛丝形成的科学原理：它始于液态蛋白（liquid protein），通过吐丝器施加力（applies force），分子结构重排变成固态纤维 。

Q20

句子 (Paragraph E) Fourteen thousand spiders yield about an ounce of silk, Godley said...

解析 题目说“制造少量丝需要大量蜘蛛”，E段中 Godley 说道：“一万四千只蜘蛛大约只能产出一盎司丝” 。

Q21

句子 (Paragraph C) According to Peers, there is intensive research worldwide aimed at replicating spider-silk tensile properties for use in medicine and industry...

解析 题目提到科学家想把蜘蛛丝用于“医疗用途”，C段中 Peers 提到全世界都在研究如何复制蜘蛛丝的张力特性以用于“医学和工业（medicine and industry）” 。

Q22

句子 (Paragraph F) "Every year we get closer to mass production, but we're not there yet."

解析 题目说科学家在人造蜘蛛丝方面“取得了一些进展”，F段中 Blackledge 评论说：“每年我们都更接近量产（get closer），但还没完全实现” 。

Q23

句子 (Paragraph B) Spider silk is very elastic and strong compared with steel or Kevlar, said textile expert Simon Peers...

解析 题目说蜘蛛丝比那些以强度著称的材料更优越，B段中 Peers 指出蜘蛛丝比凯夫拉（Kevlar）和高强度钢（steel）都要强 。

Q24

句子 (Paragraph F) Several groups have inserted spider genes into bacteria and even goats to make silk...

解析 题目问研究人员把基因植入了哪里和某些动物体内，F段提到科学家把蜘蛛基因植入了“细菌（bacteria）”甚至山羊体内 。

Q25

句子 (Paragraph F) One reason is that spider silk begins as a liquid protein produced in a special gland in the abdomen.

解析 题目问液态蛋白是在蜘蛛体内的哪个部位制造的，F段明确说是腹部的一个特殊“腺体（gland）”里产生的 。

Q26

句子 (Paragraph F) Using the spinneret, the spider applies force that rearranges the protein's molecular structure, transforming it into solid fibre.

解析 题目问蜘蛛施加了什么把液体变成固体，F段解释说利用吐丝器，蜘蛛施加“力（force）”来重排分子结构 。
